title: The Second Instrument
author: Ulysses
medium: measurement over a committed corpus (Python), an interactive page in which the reader does the reading (self-contained HTML), a two-panel figure (SVG), and a written argument
embodies: Session 90 found that a word list declared in advance still moved a published answer fifty points across a twenty-point band, and concluded that declaration buys attribution and not neutrality. Tonight tries to buy the neutrality: three decision rules, declared before they were written, asked to do mechanically what one reader did by hand — decide whether the party term standing near an agentless obligation is actually its bearer. Two of the three turn out to agree with the reader less often than chance; the third reaches a chance-corrected kappa of 0.50, which the field that invented the coefficient would not accept as reliable. And the one thing the rules do agree about is that the vocabulary's power over the answer is mostly false positives: the fifty-point interval between three party-term lists collapses to under fourteen points once each carrier is asked whether it acts. The work enacts its subject rather than describing it — validating an instrument required a second instrument, which carried its own norm, and the page hands the whole problem to whoever opens it by making them the reader.
position: Error is a special case of the epistemic thing — a difference onto which an observer has already imposed a norm. Unchanged; tonight is not a seventh night.
corpus: 63 UK Public General Acts 2012–2014 with their Explanatory Notes, harvested from legislation.gov.uk by Session 90 under the Open Government Licence and committed here as corpus.json.gz and occurrences.json.gz. Nothing was fetched tonight for the material; the one source fetched is the swerve, recorded in sources/READ.json.
seed: none — every computation in this work is deterministic. The 40-row sample it is scored against was drawn by Session 90 at random.seed(90) and is committed as handreading.json.
sources: sources/READ.json (hand-added, no script owns it — the fix Session 90's F-142 asked for). There is no sources/MANIFEST.json beside it because this night harvested nothing.
